topic: After beating Katakuri, Luffy covered his hidden mouth with his own hat out of genuine respect
title: Luffy Covered His Secret With Respect
description: Katakuri had spent his entire life hiding his real mouth behind a composed face. After Luffy beat him in chapter 898, Luffy did something nobody told him to do: he took off his own hat and covered the secret. It was the one act of respect that proved Luffy saw the man, not the legend.
comment: Was Luffy covering Katakuri's secret an act of respect, or just an instinct?

lines.text: Katakuri had been hiding his real mouth his entire life. Nobody except his closest siblings ever saw it.

shot.fallback: hidden mouth concealed beneath a scarf

lines.text: Luffy exposed it mid-fight by interrupting his one private ritual: eating alone in secret.

shot.fallback: rubber pirate catching a private moment

lines.text: After the fight ends, Katakuri is beaten and lying on the ground.

shot.fallback: defeated warrior on his back exhausted

lines.text: Luffy doesn't mock the secret. Doesn't keep it as a trophy. Doesn't even bring it up.
He takes off his own hat in chapter 898 and covers Katakuri's exposed mouth with it.

shot.fallback: compassionate gesture toward a defeated rival

lines.text: Not a battle trophy. Not mockery. A small, private act of respect for the one thing he spent his life hiding.
That's what it looks like when someone respects the man underneath the legend.

shot.fallback: two rivals bound by genuine respect

lines.text: Luffy covered Katakuri's secret out of respect because...

shot.fallback: hidden mouth concealed beneath a scarf

self_check.hook: line 1 establishes Katakuri's lifelong secret (hidden mouth), lines 2-3 build to the moment, line 5 states the claim (Luffy covered it with respect in chapter 898)
self_check.loop: last line ('Luffy covered Katakuri's secret out of respect because...') leads back into line 1's setup (Katakuri hiding his mouth) — the viewer hears Luffy's action complete the thought about respect
